active.F_179.py: fman_keygen.c: F-179 (2026-08-07), follow-up while resolving <combine>/PORT_ID against vendor's real, pristine FMC compiler source (github.com/nxp-qoriq/fmc @ 5b9f4b16a864e9dfa58cdcc860be278a7f66ac18, the exact commit this project's own fmc_git.bb pins). That trace definitively found <combine> builds KeyGen's extractedOrs (FQID-only), correcting an earlier doc claim it was a GEC key mechanism -- and while closing out that context, found KG_SCH_KN_PORT_ID (EKFC bit 31, the real key-extraction path, unrelated to <combine>) draws its value from kgse_dv0/kgse_dv1 (fm_pcd_ext.h's t_FmPcdExtractEntry has no dedicated union member for PORT_PRIVATE_INFO; vendor's fm_kg.c BuildSchemeRegs() assigns kgse_dv0/dv1 straight from the scheme's privateDflt0/1 fields). This project's own fman_keygen.c (mainline-derived, unmodified for this logic) populates kgse_dv0/dv1 with DEFAULT_HASH_KEY_IPv4_ADDR/DEFAULT_HASH_KEY_L4_PORT (0x0A0A0A0A/0x0B0B0B0B) inside the `if (scheme->use_hashing)` branch -- an unrelated mainline RSS-hashing-fallback mechanism. Live-read on .185 scheme 4 confirmed an exact byte-for-byte match. This project's own EKFC override never reprograms these registers, so both existing PORT_ID board measurements (the 2026-07-13 184,320-candidate brute force and the 2026-08-07 16-candidate 0x00-0x0f sweep) were run against this uncontrolled value -- neither result can be trusted to rule the mechanism out. Fix: zero kgse_dv0/kgse_dv1/kgse_ekdv whenever this project's own EKFC override (scheme->ekfc) is in control, so any PORT_ID extraction reads a known 0x00 instead of a leftover RSS constant, making a portid=0x00 retest genuinely controlled for the first time. Dry-run tested (including idempotency) against the exact reconstructed source text before commit.
active.F_199.py: dpaa_eth.c/.h + dpaa_flow_offload.h: F-199 (2026-08-16, T-M7-2 S4 no-confirm TX FQ; silicon-validated 2026-08-24) -- adds FQ_TYPE_TX_NO_CONFIRM + exported dpaa_alloc_offload_tx_fq() programming NXP SDK FQ_FLAG_NO_TXCONFIRM context_a 0x9a000000c0000000. Board .185 image 0500 at 7.76 Gbit/s bidirectional HIT (13.6 GB/~9.7M frames): tx-confirm totals moved only +9/+5 control-plane frames, F-227 stayed 0, board idle; the earlier 0x1c00000080000000 B0V-cleared guess generated ~600K confirms/s. Kernel's own confirm-enabled TX FQs remain untouched; F-232 proof diagnostic retired after validation.
active.F_201.py: fman_keygen.c: F-201 (2026-08-17, software-forwarding multicore fix) -- guards F-051's unconditional `kgse_hc = 0` clear on the active engine role so RSS/direct-enqueue and policer schemes (next_engine 0/1) keep the 128-FQ CRC-64 distribution computed by keygen_port_hashing_init(), while CC/FE exact-match schemes (next_engine 2/3) still get kgse_hc=0. Board-confirmed root cause on .185: F-051 collapsed all five RSS schemes (0-4) to range=0/HMASK=0 = 1 FQ, funnelling every hashed flow to the base FQ (eth3 0x200 / eth4 0x300) -> single QMan portal -> CPU0, capping software (nft flowtable) forwarding at ~2.5 Gbps with CPU0 100% softirq and millions of rx_dropped on CPU0 while CPU1-3 idle. XPS masks disproven as the fix (RX-side funnel, not TX). Runs after F-051 and F-183 (both emit the identical kgse_hc-clear line); ehash terminal ignores FQID distribution by design (spec S5.4). S0 qdrant-gated (RM Ch.5 / microcode ref kgse_fqb range + kgse_hc HMASK / BSP 128-FQ default).
active.F_203.py: dpaa_eth.c: F-203 (2026-08-17, contiguous jumbo RX) -- raises the DPAA RX buffer pool from order-0/4KiB to order-1/8KiB via DPAA_BP_ORDER=1 and DPAA_BP_RAW_SIZE=(4096<<order); changes the one RX pool dev_alloc_pages() and all eight RX-buffer free_pages() sites to the matching order while deliberately leaving TX-SGT and XDP-copy scratch pages order-0. Keeps large frames contiguous and ASK-FE-offloadable (unlike RX SG), raises usable one-buffer MTU to ~7.5K; VyOS clamps conservatively to 7000. skb_free_frag compound-head recycle remains valid. S0 qdrant-gated against the 4K-wedge record, RX SG consumer semantics, A050385 runtime-inactive on LS1046A, and BMan sizing.
